description: Original stable_marriage mod.rs and bounded models
state: Two equal-sized populations with complete strict n-entry permutation rows; total 2*n*n entries at most 2000000. Empty populations allowed.
cost: Validation, rank construction and at most n squared proposals cost O(n squared); ranks use O(n squared) auxiliary storage and queues/mates O(n). Budget arithmetic is checked before allocation; allocation failure is untyped.
forward: Validate equal sizes, checked quadratic budget, then proposer and receiver rows. Build receiver inverse ranks. FIFO free proposers propose to the next untried receiver; a receiver retains its best proposal so far and requeues the rejected proposer. Return receiver index per proposer when the queue empties.
inverse: Universe: two preference matrices crossed with candidate receiver vectors and errors. Absent successful behaviors include a non-permutation, a blocking pair (p,r) where both prefer each other to assigned mates, or a stable permutation giving a proposer a worse partner than another stable permutation. Invalid row lengths/permutations cannot succeed. Unequal sizes beat the budget error, which beats malformed rows; within each row, length beats duplicate/out-of-range entry. The finite exhaustive oracle supports these exact source-derived constraints without a general Rust proof.

For an observed permutation m, retain every pair of complete preference matrices for which m is stable and proposer-optimal: for each stable alternative s and proposer p, rank_p(m[p]) <= rank_p(s[p]). This finite relational characterization is ambiguous: with two proposers each ranking a distinct receiver first, either strict ordering in each receiver row still yields m. Observing a matching loses unproposed suffixes and proposal/rejection history. Error preimages comprise all profiles sharing the first failed validation predicate and observed indices.
limitations: Finite evidence, not proof; allocation failure unmodeled.
Partial syntax, no macro expansion or semantic AST.
